## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Don't merge this yet. `--json` treats whatever argument comes next as its path, even when that argument is another flag. So `--json` only works when it is the last argument or has an explicit path. That conflicts with the PR's goal of letting `--json` sit alongside `--junit`.

## Critical
- app/cli.py:15 — correctness — When anything follows `--json`, the code makes it the JSON destination. It checks only `i + 1 < len(args)`, not whether the next argument starts with `--`. For `["--json", "--junit", "x.xml"]`, `options["json"]` becomes `"--junit"`, then `x.xml` hits the `else` branch and raises `ValueError("unknown option: x.xml")`. The comment at app/cli.py:12 says the default applies "when no path is supplied", but it doesn't here. Could you add the same `not args[i + 1].startswith("--")` check that `--junit` uses at app/cli.py:7, to both lines 15 and 18? A test for `parse_args(["--json", "--junit", "x.xml"]) == {"json": "results.json", "junit": "x.xml"}` would cover it. — Combining the default JSON destination with `--junit` fails every time, which is the use case the PR describes. With a following flag that takes no value, `write_reports` would instead write the JSON report to a file literally named after that flag, such as `--junit`.
